name: Street pavement maintenance
summary: About $3 million for pavement maintenance and for park and street-median capital replacement was removed from the General Fund to balance the FY 2025/26 budget.
detail: The City Manager's March 30, 2026 letter says the cut "was required to balance the budget" and that waiting to repair infrastructure raises later costs.
cut_amount_note: Combined figure for pavement maintenance and park and street-median capital replacement.
action_label: Report a street problem to the City
source_title: City Manager letter to Sen. Wahab and Asm. Lee, March 30, 2026

name: Park and street-median capital replacement
address: 3300 Capitol Ave, Building B, Fremont, CA 94538
location_note: Parks & Recreation offices, City Hall Building B
summary: Capital replacement for parks and street medians was reduced as part of the same roughly $3 million General Fund cut that covered pavement maintenance.
detail: The City's February 13, 2026 release describes it as infrastructure maintenance spending reduced by approximately $3 million to balance the FY 2025/26 budget.
cut_amount_note: Included in the roughly $3 million listed under street pavement maintenance; the City does not publish a separate figure.
action_label: Report a park or median problem to the City
source_title: City Manager letter to Sen. Wahab and Asm. Lee, March 30, 2026

name: Police Department administrative staffing
summary: Six full-time administrative positions in the Police Department were eliminated in the February 10, 2026 budget rebalancing.
detail: The City says no reductions were made to current sworn police positions, that positions were eliminated or reclassified, and that no layoffs were anticipated.
cut_amount_note: Part of the $3.8 million in operational reductions across all departments.
source_title: City Council Approves Budget Rebalancing (City of Fremont, Feb 13, 2026)

name: Fremont Detention Facility staffing
summary: Two detention officer positions and one detention supervisor position were eliminated in the February 10, 2026 budget rebalancing.
detail: The City says the personnel reductions involve eliminating or reclassifying positions and that no layoffs were anticipated.
cut_amount_note: Part of the $3.8 million in operational reductions across all departments.
source_title: City Council Approves Budget Rebalancing (City of Fremont, Feb 13, 2026)

name: Department operations: staffing, overtime, training and contract services
summary: Every City department reduced spending by its share of $3.8 million in new labor costs ($3.1 million of it in the General Fund). The reductions cover staffing, overtime, training and contract services.
detail: The largest reductions were in Police, Fire and Maintenance Operations, which make up most of the General Fund. The City has not published which contract services or programs changed.
cut_amount_note: Total for all departments; it includes the police and detention positions listed separately.
source_title: City Council Approves Budget Rebalancing (City of Fremont, Feb 13, 2026)

name: Fire Department operations budget
address: 3300 Capitol Ave, Building A, Fremont, CA 94538
location_note: Fire Administration, City Hall Building A
summary: Fire is one of the three departments with the largest reductions in the February 2026 rebalancing. No reductions were made to current sworn fire positions.
detail: A March 30, 2026 City letter adds that one more fire company recommended by the department's Standards of Coverage report is not funded.
cut_amount_note: Part of the $3.8 million in operational reductions across all departments.
source_title: City Council Approves Budget Rebalancing (City of Fremont, Feb 13, 2026)

name: Human Services safety-net programs
address: 3300 Capitol Ave, Building B, Fremont, CA 94538
location_note: Human Services Department, City Hall Building B
summary: The City says State and federal funding changes will require eliminating 10 more positions in the Human Services Department, which provides safety-net services.
detail: Separately, the FY 2026/27 Proposed Budget shows Human Services staffing going from 82.7 to 79.9 full-time-equivalent positions (a change of 2.8, in funds other than the General Fund). The City has not said which programs are affected.
cut_amount_note: The City has not published a dollar figure.
source_title: City Manager letter to Sen. Wahab and Asm. Lee, March 30, 2026

name: Homelessness response services
address: 3300 Capitol Ave, Building B, Fremont, CA 94538
location_note: Human Services Department, City Hall Building B
summary: The FY 2025/26 budget kept funding the existing level of homelessness services, about $8 million, and moved $667,000 among programs.
detail: That included $150,000 more for Keep Fremont Housed and $128,000 in new funding for overdose prevention and substance use services. This is the status as of the City Manager's message after the June 10, 2025 adoption; we found no later change in the sources checked.
source_title: Community Message from the City Manager on the FY 2025/26 Operating Budget

name: Age Well Center at Lake Elizabeth
hours: Mon–Fri 8:00 am–4:30 pm, except City holidays
summary: Classes, meals and services for adults 55 and older. Listed as open with regular hours on the City's Aging and Family Services page.
detail: We found no budget-related change for this center in the City sources checked. Call to confirm before visiting.
source_title: Aging and Family Services (City of Fremont)

name: Age Well Center at South Fremont
hours: Mon–Fri 8:00 am–4:30 pm, except City holidays
summary: Classes, meals and services for adults 55 and older. Listed as open with regular hours on the City's Aging and Family Services page.
detail: We found no budget-related change for this center in the City sources checked. Call to confirm before visiting.

name: Youth and Family Services counseling
address: 39155 Liberty St, Suite E500, Fremont, CA 94538
location_note: Inside the Fremont Family Resource Center
summary: Individual and family counseling for Fremont youth and families, with fees on a sliding scale. Listed as open on the City's Youth and Family Services page.
detail: The City lists counseling in Spanish, Farsi, Mandarin, Urdu, Marathi and Hebrew and notes that language capacity can change. We found no budget-related change for this program in the City sources checked.
